title: Tenali and the Wooden Horse

full_text:
A boastful foreign carpenter and toy-maker named Shilpi Somappa arrived at King Krishnadevaraya’s court with an intricately carved, life-size wooden horse painted in glittering gold and emerald lacquer.
Somappa claimed:
'Jahanpanah! This is no ordinary wooden toy! It is an enchanted "Celestial Flying Steed"!
Inside its belly is a complex mechanism of bronze gears and clockwork springs.
When the master pilot presses the secret silver peg behind its left ear, the horse will flap its mechanical wings, rise into the clouds, and fly across five hundred leagues in a single hour!
I offer this military marvel to Your Majesty for ten thousand gold dinars!'

King Krishnadevaraya and his generals were fascinated. The thought of an aerial warhorse that could fly over enemy fortress walls was intoxicating.
The King was on the verge of handing over the ten thousand gold coins when Tenali Raman spoke:
'Maharaj, this is indeed an extraordinary invention! Let us witness its flight before paying the gold.'

The carpenter began to stammer:
'Your Majesty, the mechanism is delicate; it requires an auspicious planetary alignment, which will not occur for six months! But if you pay the ten thousand coins now, I will complete the tuning!'

Tenali smiled with dazzling enthusiasm:
'Nonsense, Master Shilpi! The stars are in magnificent alignment today!
In fact, I shall pilot the flying horse myself!'

Tenali leaped onto the back of the wooden horse in the palace courtyard.
He grabbed the painted reins, found the silver peg behind the ear, and pressed it firmly!
Nothing happened. The heavy wooden horse remained completely stationary upon the stone tiles.

Tenali shouted: 'Fly, celestial steed! Rise into the clouds!'
He bounced up and down upon the wooden saddle, making loud whinnying sounds:
*‘NEIGH! CLOP-CLOP! FLY TO THE CLOUDS!’*
The horse did not move an inch.

Tenali then turned to the carpenter:
'Ah! Perhaps the horse requires its creator’s magical touch!
Master Shilpi, mount the horse behind me! We shall fly together from the top of the seven-story palace tower!
Guards, carry this wooden horse to the highest parapet of the fortress tower, so Master Shilpi can demonstrate its flight by jumping into the air!'

The carpenter turned pale as a corpse!
He threw himself onto his knees, trembling, clutching the King's feet:
'Mercy, Maharaj! Do not throw me from the tower!
The horse cannot fly! It is only hollow cedar wood and cheap iron springs! I forged the mechanism to swindle ten thousand gold coins from the treasury!'

The court erupted in laughter at the exposed fraud.
King Krishnadevaraya reprimanded the carpenter, sentenced him to build wooden benches for public schools for a year, and praised Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, thy willingness to test flight from the tower grounded a soaring swindler in an instant!'
moral: Charlatans who promise magical machines to fleece the royal treasury are easily exposed when asked to pilot their own inventions.

quiz.question: What fundamental virtue is highlighted in "Tenali and the Wooden Horse"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in hasty anger without listening
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of the story.

quiz.question: How does the central character approach their challenge?
options: Through thoughtful reflection, patience, and presence of mind
By shouting loudly and blaming friends
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in timeless fables.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach readers?
options: Patience, honesty, and humility lead to lasting harmony
quiz.hint: Think about how justice and truth prevail.
